topSignals.title: EFCF Lucerne pre-conference day opens — Elcogen E3000 G2 debuts, technical results from tomorrow
topSignals.text: — Today (June 29) the European Fuel Cell Forum begins its pre-conference programme in Lucerne: project workshops, the Grid Service Market Symposium (GSM 2026), and Sustainable Shipping Days. The main 17th SOFC & SOE Forum opens Monday June 30 and runs through July 3, chaired by Ceres Power's Dr. Subhasish Mukerjee. Elcogen confirmed their presence to showcase the E3000 G2 stack platform (featured in the June 28 digest); first technical papers on stack efficiency, degradation rates, and manufacturing cost from Ceres licensees, Elcogen, SolydEra, and Convion are expected from Tuesday onward. EFCF programme | Elcogen at EFCF

topSignals.title: Section 179D: today is the last business day before the June 30 construction-begin sunset
topSignals.text: — Under the OBBBA, the Section 179D commercial buildings energy efficiency deduction is permanently terminated for any project that has not begun significant physical work by June 30, 2026. For co-located data center + fuel cell projects, today is the last actionable day: initiating foundation work or spending >=5% of total project cost preserves eligibility. Projects that miss the deadline still qualify for ITC 48E (30% capital credit), but lose the additional per-square-foot deduction of up to $5.81. No breaking news of last-minute groundbreakings but the deadline is live. EnergyStackHub | constructionowners.com

topSignals.title: Bloom Energy enters EFCF week at $252 — down 25% from peak — as Q2 earnings July 30 becomes the next reset
topSignals.text: — After the FCEL/BE rotation on June 26 (FCEL +27.5%, BE -18.5% to a Friday close of $252.02), Bloom heads into the EFCF conference week significantly off its $334-$351 June 17-18 all-time high. Pre-market models forecast a June 29 opening near $266 (+5.6% recovery). Q2 2026 earnings on July 30 are now the primary catalyst: consensus expects ~$820M in Q2 revenue (100%+ YoY), EPS ~$0.39, and non-GAAP gross margin ~34%. A TIKR bull case of $920/share has circulated based on the full Oracle deal expansion to 2.8 GW. Analyst range: Barclays $276 Equal Weight; UBS $322 Buy; TIKR bull $920. stockinvest.us | TIKR | TipRanks earnings

items.text: EFCF 2026 pre-conference begins — See Top Signal #1. Watch for first technical disclosures from European developers starting June 30. Key items to flag for the LCOE model: (a) any stack efficiency improvement beyond the E3000 G2's stated 75% electrical / 90% including heat; (b) degradation benchmarks from Ceres licensees at scale; (c) manufacturing cost per kW from the 360 MW ELCO I Tallinn factory vs. Bloom's Fremont benchmark. EFCF

Topsoe cancels 100 MW SOEC supply agreement with First Ammonia (March 2026, first appearance) — Topsoe terminated its deal to supply a 100 MW SOEC electrolyser stack to First Ammonia, citing weak project pipeline in the hydrogen market. Topsoe's Herning SOEC factory (500 MW/year capacity) opened in 2025, but project offtake is not keeping pace. Implication for the SOFC LCOE model: the H2-fueled SOFC pathway remains constrained by H2 supply economics; natural gas is the economic base case through at least 2028-2029. Topsoe pivots to e-SAF (Project Starling, UK, Carbon Neutral Fuels). Fuel Cells Works

Nebius + Bloom full detail (first full appearance; headline MOU noted June 24) — SEC filings confirm the May 14, 2026 partnership covers 328 MW Phase 1 (250 MW guaranteed capacity) under an Energy-as-a-Service model: Bloom installs, operates, and maintains the systems; Nebius purchases power output. Three 10-year phases total up to $2.6B in contracted service fees; first power expected in 2026 at Nebius AI data center sites. The EaaS model is strategically significant: it lowers capital barriers for AI cloud operators who prefer opex over capex, and transfers O&M risk to Bloom. SEC 6-K Nebius | CryptoBriefing | Simply Wall St
Quiet day on net-new deployment announcements. Active pipeline: Oracle/Jupiter 2.45 GW, Crusoe/Cheyenne 900 MW Phase 1, Equinix >100 MW, FCEL/Fit Energy 380 MW, Bloom/Brookfield $5B, Nebius 328 MW.

Section 179D final day — See Top Signal #2. No news of last-minute data center project groundbreakings. After June 30, ITC 48E (30% credit) remains the primary federal incentive for fuel cell installations.
Quiet day. No new FERC, ERCOT, EU CADA, or Germany EnEfG developments since June 28 coverage.

Bloom Energy (BE) — Friday June 26 close: $252.02 (down 18.49% on the session, from $309.18; -25% from the June 17-18 peak of ~$334-$351). Pre-market June 29 model: ~$266 (+5.6%). 52-week range: $21.50-$351.28. Analyst consensus: 28 analysts, avg PT $264.53 (Buy). Barclays $276 Equal Weight (Q2 preview); UBS $322 Buy; TIKR bull case $920 on full 2.8 GW Oracle deployment. Q2 earnings: July 30, 2026 (AH). Revenue consensus: ~$820M; EPS: ~$0.39; gross margin target ~34%. stockinvest.us | MarketBeat | TIKR

FuelCell Energy (FCEL) — No update since +27.5% surge June 26 (Jefferies Buy $24, UBS Neutral $22). Torrington expansion ($200-275M, 350-500 MW/year) on track. June 2026 deep-dive analysis confirms: FCEL 4 GW pipeline is primarily data-center originated; pipeline grew 275% since Feb 2025. Q3 FY2026 earnings expected ~September 2026. Merlintrader

ECS SOFC XIX Focus Issue (JES, 2026) — papers now publishing — The Journal of The Electrochemical Society focus issue linked to SOFC-XIX (Stockholm, July 2025) is actively publishing. Noteworthy paper: "Exchange Current Density in Solid Oxide Cells: A Generalized Theoretical Framework and Application to H2/H2O Reactions" — unified kinetic model for SOFC anode/cathode exchange current, applicable to degradation modeling and electrode design optimization. IOPscience | ECS call

Wiley Advanced Energy Materials (June 2026) — "Emerging Materials and Future Strategies for Solid Oxide Electrochemical Cells" — survey of perovskite electrodes, proton-conducting electrolytes (PCECs at sub-600 degrees C), and next-generation cathode materials for SOFC and SOEC; identifies protonic cells as a potential sub-600 degrees C successor pathway. Wiley
Watch: EFCF Lucerne June 30 - July 3 — Technical results from European stack developers expected from tomorrow.

lcoe.text: Topsoe SOEC slowdown: H2 supply not on track for pre-2029 SOFC fuel switch — First Ammonia 100 MW cancellation and soft SOEC pipeline confirm H2 cost/availability does not support H2-fueled SOFC scenarios before 2028-2029. Recommend keeping natural gas as the base-case fuel in all near-term LCOE scenarios; introduce H2 sensitivity only in 2029+ scenarios.

Nebius EaaS model: bundled $/MWh contract rate — The Energy-as-a-Service structure shifts O&M risk to Bloom; the effective cost to the customer is a bundled $/MWh rate. Watch for any disclosed PPA/EaaS pricing in Nebius quarterly filings — it would be the first public market reference rate for large-scale SOFC power.

BE Q2 July 30 earnings: key capex signal — If Bloom discloses manufacturing cost per kW at the 2 GW Fremont run rate, it will provide the most current large-volume SOFC system capex benchmark. Recommend updating the LCOE model cost inputs after the July 30 call.

Section 179D sunset: model impact — After today, new projects lose the 179D deduction. The 30% ITC 48E (net capex ~$4,650-5,060/kW) remains. For 179D-eligible projects completed before the deadline, the combined incentive stack could reduce effective capex by an additional $0.58-5.81/sq.ft.
